skiResultsR

Extract and analyze ski race results from skiresults.co.uk HTML files

skiResultsR provides a comprehensive set of functions for extracting structured data from ski race result HTML files generated by skiresults.co.uk. Convert race data into clean data frames for analysis, visualization, and reporting.

Features

  • 🎿 Complete Event Extraction - Extract all event data with a single function call
  • 🏁 Race Analysis - Get individual race results with cleaned times and rankings
  • 👥 Racer Information - Extract participant details with profile links and club affiliations
  • 🏆 Points Data - Analyze points across different categories and competitions
  • 📊 Clean Data Structures - Consistent data frames ready for analysis
  • 🔗 Preserve Links - Maintain hyperlinks to racer profiles and club pages

Installation 

# Install from CRAN (when available)
install.packages("skiResultsR")

# Or install development version from GitHub
devtools::install_github("yourusername/skiResultsR")

Quick Start 

library(skiResultsR)

# Get path to sample data
file_path <- system.file("extdata", "chatham_oct2023.html", package = "skiResultsR")

# Extract complete event data
event_data <- get_event(file_path)

# View event summary
print(event_data$event_summary$title)
#> [1] "Chatham Ski Slope: LSERSA (07 October 2023)"

# View available races
names(event_data$races)
#> [1] "race-9973" "race-9981" "race-9974" "race-9975" "race-9976"

# Get racers
head(event_data$racers)
#>        name                              href club club_href
#> 1 BUNTON Ryan https://skiresults.co.uk/people/30 <NA>      <NA>
#> 2  BROWN Ben  https://skiresults.co.uk/people/23 <NA>      <NA>

Main Functions

Primary Functions

Function Purpose Returns
get_event() Extract complete event data List with all components
get_races() Extract all race tables List of race data frames
get_race() Extract specific race by ID/type Single race data frame

Helper Functions

Function Purpose Returns
get_racers() Extract unique racers with links Data frame
get_race_points() Extract points across categories Data frame
get_event_summary() Extract event metadata List

Usage Examples

Get Event Summary 

# Quick event overview
summary <- get_event_summary(file_path)
cat("Event:", summary$title)
cat("Date:", summary$date)
cat("Venue:", summary$slope)

Analyze Race Performance 

# Get a specific race
race_data <- get_race(file_path, "race-9973")

# View race statistics
if ("time_cleaned" %in% names(race_data)) {
  times <- race_data$time_cleaned[!is.na(race_data$time_cleaned)]
  cat("Fastest time:", min(times), "seconds")
  cat("Average time:", mean(times), "seconds")
}

Extract Points Data 

# Get points across all categories
points <- get_race_points(file_path)

# Analyze by category
table(points$points_category)
aggregate(points ~ points_category, data = points, FUN = mean)

Data Structure

The package returns consistent, well-structured data:

event_data <- get_event(file_path)
str(event_data, max.level = 1)
#> List of 5
#>  $ event_summary: List of 8
#>  $ races        : List of 5
#>  $ racers       : 'data.frame': 150 obs. of 4 variables
#>  $ race_points  : 'data.frame': 0 obs. of 7 variables  
#>  $ clubs        : 'data.frame': 0 obs. of 2 variables

Sample Data

The package includes sample HTML files for testing and examples:

  • chatham_oct2023.html - Chatham Ski Slope event from October 2023
  • brentwood_jun2023.html - Brentwood Park event from June 2023
# List available sample files
list.files(system.file("extdata", package = "skiResultsR"))
